content.text: Repairing per the accuracy note: I'll trim the § 12.4 commentary so this finding doesn't pre-judge the non-compete conflict.

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: Compliant at the preferred position: no non-solicit binds Customer. A full section-outline sweep plus targeted searches for "solicit", "employ or engage", "induce", "recruit", "hire", "employee" and "personnel" return no non-solicitation, no-poach or no-hire covenant anywhere in the Agreement. The only responsive text, Section 12.3, runs in our favour: it preserves Meridian Fieldworks' right to hire any person who responds to general recruitment and records that we have given no no-hire commitment. Per the rule's preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer"), there is nothing to narrow, and the playbook directs us not to flag a clause that benefits our party, so no redline or counterparty comment is proposed. The failed deterministic checks (duration <= 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out) are non-probative here: both regexes look for a restriction period and a carve-out sentence inside an existing restrictive covenant, and no such covenant exists to measure. Section 12.3's general-recruitment language is in substance broader than the fallback carve-out because it is a standing freedom rather than an exception to a restriction. Restrictive covenants other than employee non-solicitation are outside the scope of this rule and are reported under their own rules; nothing in this finding is intended to resolve their scope or interaction with Section 12.3.
